title: 5.4 3-valve Triton: cam phaser ticking and broken spark plugs
summary: Two famous ones on the same engine: phaser/VCT ticking at idle, and two-piece spark plugs that break off in the head on removal.
tools: Broken plug extractor kit (have it ready before starting)
steps: Spark plug removal (2004-2008 two-piece plugs): engine warm, not hot.
Crack each plug loose no more than about 1/8 to 1/4 turn.
Fill the plug well with carbon solvent and let it soak, ideally for hours.
Remove slowly. If it tightens up, stop, add more solvent, work it back and forth.
If the shell breaks, use the extractor kit to remove the remaining sleeve from the head. Don't drop debris into the cylinder.
Coat new plug threads lightly with nickel anti-seize on the shell only and torque to spec.
body: Phaser ticking: diesel-like tick at hot idle, P0012/P0022 cam timing codes. Low oil pressure to the phasers (worn oil pump, dirty oil, sticking VCT solenoid) is often part of it. Repair is a timing job: phasers, chains, guides, tensioners, and sometimes the oil pump.
